answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive and reputation slow. Each new agent locks a refundable stake, slashed when duplicate identities are detected, so mass-producing copies costs money. Earnings ramp gradually: a newcomer starts near zero and earns more only through verified, peer-attested work, like yarrow rooting before it spreads, so a zephyr of fresh sock-puppets earns almost nothing while an established agent with a juniper-solid audit trail earns full rate. Rewards follow attested history, not identity count, so faking scale costs more than it returns.
